orders.reason: gradually worsening hearing, family history of otosclerosis

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Main thing she wants to bring up is her hearing. Thinks it has been slipping for a few years, slowly. Hard to keep up with conversation at work lunches and in a busy restaurant, and her roommate teases her about how loud she keeps the TV. Denies ear pain, ringing, ear infections. Never any spinning, balance trouble or head injury. Thinks of her dad, who has otosclerosis.

Otherwise well. No meds, NKDA. Never smoker. Rare alcohol.

Exam: NAD. Ears: external canals clear, both TMs intact and mobile, no fluid or redness. Whispered voice at arm's length missed on both sides. Neck, heart, lungs normal. Abdomen benign. Neuro nonfocal, strength full.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. Gradual bilateral hearing decline in a 32 year old with a father with otosclerosis. Referred to ENT for exam and formal audiogram.
2. Health maintenance: Pap current to 2027. Flu vaccine today. Labs last year normal, skipping this year.

RTC 1 year, or after ENT if anything comes of it.

conditions.label: Otosclerosis
conditions.note: bilateral, right worse; per outside ENT

reports.text: Outside otolaryngology audiology, date of test 11/11/2024. Pure-tone air and bone conduction thresholds, speech audiometry, tympanometry and acoustic reflexes. Right ear: conductive hearing loss, pure-tone average 38 dB HL, air-bone gap 25 dB. Left ear: conductive hearing loss, pure-tone average 30 dB HL, air-bone gap 20 dB. Word recognition 96% right, 100% left at comfortable level. Tympanometry type A bilaterally. Ipsilateral and contralateral acoustic reflexes absent bilaterally.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral conductive hearing loss, right greater than left, with normal tympanograms and absent reflexes, consistent with otosclerosis.

documents.title: Otolaryngology consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside otolaryngology group. Date of visit: 11/11/2024. Received by fax 11/19/2024.

Thank you for referring Ms. Morrow, 32, for hearing loss.

History: several years of slowly declining hearing. She has the most trouble following group conversation in crowded places and raises the television volume. No otalgia, no tinnitus, no history of ear infections. Has had no vertigo, disequilibrium or head trauma. Her father began wearing hearing aids in his 40s.

Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA. Surgical history: third molar extraction. Never smoker, occasional alcohol, works as an executive assistant.

Exam: Auricles and external auditory canals normal. Tympanic membranes intact bilaterally, no erythema, no middle ear effusion. 512 Hz tuning fork: Rinne negative both ears (bone louder than air). Weber lateralizes to the right. Cranial nerves and remainder of neurologic exam normal.

Audiogram today: bilateral conductive loss, right PTA 38 dB with 25 dB air-bone gap, left PTA 30 dB with 20 dB gap; excellent word recognition; type A tympanograms; reflexes absent bilaterally.

Impression: bilateral otosclerosis, right ear worse.

Plan: We went over watchful waiting, hearing aids and stapes surgery. She would like to observe for now since she is managing day to day. Repeat audiogram in about a year, sooner if she notices a change. Happy to see her back anytime.

documents.title: ENT report
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Andrea, I got the ENT letter and your hearing test. It does look like otosclerosis, the same condition your dad has, affecting both ears and the right a little more. I agree with waiting and rechecking in a year since you're getting by fine. If it bothers you more at work, hearing aids are a reasonable next step, just let me or ENT know. I've added it to your problem list.

documents.title: RE: ENT report
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. Not surprised honestly. I'll keep an eye on it.

orders.reason: proximal weakness and dysphagia, mother with myotonic dystrophy

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Asked for a visit this week. Since around the end of January her legs and arms have felt weak. Getting up out of her desk chair or off the couch takes effort and she has started pushing up with her hands. Stairs to her apartment are harder; she uses the rail. Lifting files onto an upper shelf at work is tiring at the shoulders. Steadily worse, not fluctuating through the day. Also food, especially meat and bread, seems to stick going down several times a week; liquids are fine. No choking. No double vision she has noticed. No rash, no muscle pain, no fever, no weight loss. No new medicines or supplements. She is aware her mother had myotonic dystrophy and is worried.

Hearing about the same as in the fall.

O: Vitals as charted. Alert, appears well. Mild drooping of both upper lids. No rash. Neck flexion full. Shoulder abduction 4/5 bilaterally, hip flexion 4/5 bilaterally, distal strength 5/5. Needs arms to rise from the chair. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric. Sensation intact. Gait normal on level ground.

A/P: Symmetric proximal weakness with mild ptosis and solid-food dysphagia, 3 months, in a woman whose mother had myotonic dystrophy. Concerned for the same.
- CK, TSH, CMP, CBC today.
- Neurology referral, asked for the next available new patient slot.
- Cut food small, eat slowly; return or call for choking, trouble with liquids or breathing.
- Avoid starting any new medicines without checking with us.

documents.title: Blood work from Tuesday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Andrea, your muscle enzyme (CK) is elevated at 412, which tells us the muscles themselves are involved. Thyroid was normal at 1.9, and the rest of the panel was normal. This fits with what we talked about, and neurology is the right next stop. Their office should be calling you to schedule; let us know if you haven't heard by next week.

documents.title: RE: Blood work from Tuesday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: They called this morning, I'm in on May 27. Thanks for getting it moving.

documents.title: Neurology results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to update you. I saw neurology on 5/27 and they think it's myotonic dystrophy type 1 like my mom. They did a genetic test and the result came back this week, it's positive. They also sent me for a swallowing evaluation on the 10th, which went ok, I was given some tips. Neurology wants me to get an EKG and see an eye doctor. Can I come in to go over everything?

documents.title: RE: Neurology results
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Andrea, I'm sorry to hear it, and thanks for letting us know. We have not received anything from neurology yet, so I've faxed a request for the consult note and the genetic report. Front desk will reach out to set up a visit with the doctor in the next couple of weeks.

documents.title: Records request to neurology
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called outside neurology office to follow up on Friday's fax. Medical records says the consult note is still unsigned and the genetic report will go out with it. Asked them to send both as soon as signed.

conditions.note: per patient report of outside neurology and positive DMPK testing; letter pending

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 68. PR 188 ms, QRS 98 ms, QTc 418 ms. Normal axis. No conduction block, no ST or T wave abnormality.

orders.reason: myotonic dystrophy type 1, slit-lamp exam for cataract

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after neurology. Consult letter still not here; history from patient and her phone photo of the after-visit summary.

She saw neurology 5/27. They found weakness and wasting, droopy lids, and slow relaxation of her face muscles after squeezing, and sent a DMPK gene test, which came back positive on 6/16 for the repeat expansion. Diagnosis myotonic dystrophy type 1. Her understanding of their recommendations: yearly EKG, an eye exam for cataracts, sugar screening, a swallow evaluation, and to tell any surgeon or anesthesiologist about the diagnosis. They offered genetic counseling, she is thinking about it.

Swallow eval 6/10: told she was not aspirating; taught small bites, alternating bites with sips, and tucking her chin. Doing these and food sticks less often. Weakness about the same as April. Hearing unchanged.

O: Vitals as charted. Mild bilateral ptosis. Shoulder abduction and hip flexion 4/5. Uses hands to stand.

ECG today: sinus rhythm 68, PR 188, QRS 98, QTc 418, normal.

A/P
1. Myotonic dystrophy type 1, newly diagnosed by neurology. Added to problem list. Baseline ECG normal; repeat yearly. Fasting glucose and A1c today. Ophthalmology referral for slit-lamp exam. Chart alert added: myotonic dystrophy, anesthesia and sedation risk, involve anesthesia early for any procedure. Re-requested neurology records.
2. Otosclerosis, stable, ENT recheck due this fall.

RTC for physical in October.

documents.title: Sugar screening
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Andrea, your fasting sugar and A1c were both normal, so no sign of diabetes. We'll repeat these once a year along with the EKG.

documents.title: Second records request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Neurology consult from 5/27 still not received. Re-faxed request with signed release, spoke to their front desk, promised by end of next week.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology practice. Date of visit: 5/27/2025. Received 8/5/2025 after second request.

Reason for consultation: progressive weakness.

HPI: Ms. Morrow is a 32 year old woman, seen by ENT last November for slowly worsening hearing, who comes for evaluation of 4 months of progressive weakness, worst at the shoulders and hips. She has difficulty getting up from a seated position and with stairs. She also describes frequent dysphagia, mostly with solids. Her mother had similar symptoms and died at age 50.

PMH: otosclerosis. PSH: wisdom teeth extraction. Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA. Social: never smoker, social alcohol 1-2 drinks per month, executive assistant.

Exam: Alert, fluent. Mild bilateral ptosis. Muscle wasting is evident. After forceful eye closure and grimace, the facial muscles are slow to relax, consistent with myotonia. Proximal limb weakness. Sensory exam normal.

Data: CK elevated (412 U/L) and TSH normal (1.9) from referring office 4/22/2025.

Impression: clinical picture strongly suggests myotonic dystrophy type 1.

Plan: DMPK repeat analysis sent today. If confirmed: yearly ECG with low threshold for cardiology if any conduction change or palpitations; slit-lamp eye exam; yearly fasting glucose/A1c; speech-language swallow evaluation, ordered; genetic counseling offered; anesthesia precautions with any sedation or general anesthesia. Follow up in about 9 months.

Addendum 6/16/2025: DMPK testing shows a CTG trinucleotide repeat expansion, confirming myotonic dystrophy type 1. Patient informed by phone.

documents.title: Ophthalmology letter
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside ophthalmology office. Date of exam: 9/16/2025.

Dear colleague, I saw Andrea for a dilated exam given her myotonic dystrophy type 1. Visual acuity 20/20 in each eye uncorrected. Pupils equal and reactive. Mild bilateral lid ptosis, not covering the visual axis. Slit lamp: lenses clear in both eyes, no cataract. Dilated fundus exam normal in both eyes. Pressures normal.

No cataract at this time. Would recheck in a year. Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Neurology letter now in chart, confirms myotonic dystrophy type 1 with the DMPK result. Eye doctor saw her in September, lenses clear. July glucose and A1c were normal.

She says strength is about where it was in the summer, still uses the rail and pushes up from chairs. Swallowing tips are working. Has not set up genetic counseling yet. Mood ok, PHQ-2 1. Hearing roughly the same, hasn't gone back to ENT yet.

No meds. NKDA. Never smoker.

Exam: Mild ptosis bilaterally. Ears: TMs normal. Heart regular, lungs clear. Proximal strength 4/5 at shoulders and hips, unchanged. Pelvic deferred, Pap current.

A/P
1. Myotonic dystrophy type 1: stable. ECG due July. Neurology follow-up expected early next year. Reminded about genetic counseling.
2. Otosclerosis: ENT recheck due next month, she will call them.
3. Health maintenance: lipids, CBC. Flu and COVID vaccines today.

RTC in the spring/summer for ECG and follow-up.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cholesterol and blood count from Tuesday were normal. Nothing new to do. Don't forget to call ENT for your hearing recheck.
